rv.q: You hear his screams and the squelch of metal on flesh. But the blood-letting becomes explicit, and graphic, albeit with a surprising, stylised twist (which should not be given away).

And after seeing the production… well, I can confirm they’re probably a good idea, just in case of any splashes. But this isn’t just Shakespeare’s bloodiest play; it’s a bloody good production of the bloodiest play. Thankfully though, while it is bloody, it’s not actually particularly gory.
